# Software Specification: Helios Bundle Draft Format

## 1. Core Format & Structure (The 2-Round Block Blueprint)

* **Variable Player Count:** The draft natively supports a completely flexible number of players (natively scaling to any lobby size), though it is optimized for exactly 8 players to achieve the ideal card game pod feel.
* **The Fixed Pack Size Rule:** Every pack generated by the software contains an absolute fixed number of exactly 15 items (bundles in Round 1, single cards in Round 2), completely independent of how many players join the lobby.
* **The Turn Pacing:** Each round consists of 15 consecutive parallel passes. A round ends only when the 15 items in the packs are completely empty.
    * *The 8-Player Wheel:* If playing with the optimized 8 players, a player makes their 1st pick, the pack circles the table, and wheels back onto their screen on pick 9 with exactly 7 items left for their 2nd choice.
* **The Total Draft Stability:** Regardless of the player count, every player at the table will make exactly 30 total picks across the entire draft (15 picks in Round 1, 15 picks in Round 2), standardizing final collection sizes.
* **The Strictly Hidden Information Rule:** All drafted cards—including specific Extra Deck monsters and archetype bundles—go directly into a player's private digital binder. No picked cards are ever revealed to opponents during the draft. Players must deduce what their neighbors are drafting entirely by reading the signals of what is missing from passed packs, creating a deep layer of deduction for competitive team play.
* **The 1-Block Sequence (2 Rounds Total):**
    * *Round 1 (Archetype & Engine Bundles):* Contains 15 pre-constructed hidden synergy bundles. A bundle consists of a core engine of Main Deck cards, plus any specific, required Extra Deck boss monsters hard-coded directly into that bundle.
    * *Round 2 (Generic Utility Singles):* Contains 15 individual single cards consisting purely of generic, high-utility Extra Deck toolbox monsters and universally playable Main Deck tech/spells/traps.
* **Direction of Pass:**
    * Round 1 passes to the Left.
    * Round 2 passes to the Right.

---

## 2. Pack Composition & Bundle Syntax

### A. Round 1 Packs (Archetype & Engine Bundles)
* **The Item Count:** Every Round 1 pack generated by the software contains exactly 15 hidden bundles.
* **The Size Constraint:** The number of cards inside each bundle is variable, with the strict structural rule that no bundle can contain fewer than 2 cards.
* **The Structural Diversity:** Bundles can freely scale from 2-card micro-packages up to massive, multi-card archetype cores.

### B. Round 2 Packs (Generic Utility Singles)
* **The Item Count:** Every Round 2 pack generated by the software contains exactly 15 individual single cards.
* **The Card Types:** Every slot is treated as an independent choice consisting purely of generic, high-utility Extra Deck toolbox monsters and universally playable Main Deck spells, traps, or tech cards.

---

## 3. The Pick Phase & Sorting Logic

* **The Selection Rule:** On a player's turn, they select exactly ONE item from the pack currently on their screen (one bundle in Round 1, or one single card in Round 2). Locking in the choice claims all cards contained within that item.
* **The Secret Binder:** When an item is drafted, its contents are instantly transferred into the player's private digital binder. To maintain the Strictly Hidden Information rule, no opponent can ever see what cards or bundles another player has selected.
* **Live Pool Sorting (UI Layout):** During the draft, players have real-time access to view their own drafted pool. The software automatically filters and sorts their claimed cards into separate, organized visual tabs to facilitate strategic planning on subsequent picks:
    * *Main Deck Tab:* Displays all drafted Main Deck monsters, spells, and traps.
    * *Extra Deck Tab:* Displays all drafted Fusion, Synchro, Xyz, and Link monsters.
* **Bundle Re-Clumping Feature:** The UI includes a toggle or button that allows players to instantly group their drafted cards back into their original, pre-constructed bundle packages. This helps players visually track which cohesive engines they have successfully claimed throughout the draft.
* **Asynchronous Queue Flow:** Picks do not require synchronized table-wide lock-ins. As soon as a player locks in their selection, the software immediately passes the remaining items to the next player's queue. If a player is drafting slowly, passed packs will automatically accumulate as a waiting stack on their screen, while faster players can continue drafting without waiting.

---

## 4. Deck Construction & Gameplay Errata

* **Main Deck Size Constraints:** Final constructed decks must meet a strict minimum of exactly 30 cards. There is no upper limit up to the maximum total number of Main Deck cards drafted.
* **Extra Deck Size Constraints:** The final Extra Deck cannot exceed a maximum of exactly 15 cards.
* **The Sideboard (Unlimited Size):** All remaining drafted cards (Main Deck or Extra Deck) that are not included in the starting deck automatically form the player's Sideboard. Unlike a standard Yu-Gi-Oh! side deck, this sideboard has no maximum size limit and can contain any number of cards up to the total remainder of the player's drafted pool. Players may freely swap cards between games in a match following standard Yu-Gi-Oh! sideboard rules.
* **The 3-Copy Limit Abolished:** The official Yu-Gi-Oh! rule restricting players to a maximum of 3 copies of any individual card is completely lifted. Players are legally allowed to run 4 or more copies of a single card in their Main or Extra Deck if they managed to draft them across multiple bundles.
* **Cube Legality Precedence:** All card interactions, mechanics, and individual card bans are dictated entirely by the curated card pool uploaded by the cube manager. Official TCG/OCG Banlists are overridden by the custom environment.
